claim_title: ?sort= is silently ignored by three paged endpoints; /api/vocabulary honours it and returns 500 on an unknown property
rate_limit_prep: docker exec engflow-redis redis-cli --scan --pattern 'rate_limit:*' | del — flushed before probes

part_1_unknown_property_500.body: {"detail":"Tham số sắp xếp không hợp lệ.","instance":"/api/vocabulary","status":400,"title":"Bad Request"}
part_1_unknown_property_500.backend_log: WARN c.d.e.exception.GlobalExceptionHandler : Invalid sort property: No property 'notacolumn' found for type 'Vocabulary'
part_1_unknown_property_500.why: The live working tree already contains an uncommitted fix: GlobalExceptionHandler.handlePropertyReferenceException(...) -> ProblemDetail 400, documented in-source as 'audit-v13 F-13-11'. It is in `git diff` (+17 lines) but NOT in HEAD (`git show HEAD:...GlobalExceptionHandler.java | grep PropertyReferenceException` -> empty). The claim was recorded BEFORE the fix and was never re-measured after it.
part_1_unknown_property_500.existing_evidence_in_repo: evidence/f13-11-13-verify.json records F-13-11_invalid_sort {before:500, after:400} and evidence/api-sweep.md F-13-01c already states the same 500. The claim under review is a stale copy of an already-fixed item.

part_2_sort_ignored_three_endpoints.lessons: GET /api/lessons?size=5&sort=title,asc vs ,desc -> IDENTICAL payloads: [(41881,'test'),(81895,'Admin Created Lesson'),(91900,...),(91919,'test'),(91920,'thầy bình ')]; totalElements=1465; both HTTP 200
part_2_sort_ignored_three_endpoints.admin_exercises: GET /api/admin/exercises?size=5&sort=title,asc vs ,desc (admin token) -> IDENTICAL, ids [766149,766150,777434,745554,745559]; both HTTP 200
part_2_sort_ignored_three_endpoints.decks: GET /api/decks?size=5&sort=name,asc vs ,desc (user token) -> IDENTICAL, names ['Academic Word List','Common English Idioms','Essential Phrasal Verbs','Everyday English','IELTS Academic: Environment']; both HTTP 200
part_2_sort_ignored_three_endpoints.source_confirmed: LessonController:38 PageRequest.of(..., Sort.by("orderIndex").ascending().and(Sort.by("id"))); AdminExerciseController:39 Sort.by("orderIndex"); DeckController:34,50 Sort.by("name"). All three build their own PageRequest and never read ?sort=. VocabularyController:37 binds @PageableDefault(size=20, sort="word") Pageable.
part_2_sort_ignored_three_endpoints.is_this_a_bug: No actionable defect. (a) Zero frontend callers send ?sort= to any of these endpoints — `grep -rn 'sort=' frontend/src` returns no hits, so the parameter is unused. (b) The hardcoded order is deliberate and meaningful (orderIndex = curriculum order; name = alphabetical deck list), so the 200 default order is the correct, stable response, not a silent wrong answer to a real request.

part_3_word_drop_500.body: {"detail":"Đã xảy ra lỗi hệ thống. Vui lòng thử lại sau.","instance":"/api/vocabulary","status":500,"title":"Internal Server Error"}
part_3_word_drop_500.note: This is a DIFFERENT exception class from the fixed one — the sort string 'word;DROP' is not parsed as a property reference, so PropertyReferenceException never fires and it falls through to the catch-all 500. Real, but: no SQL injection (sort is mapped to a JPA property path, never concatenated), no data loss (parity table intact), requires authentication, and no frontend caller sends a sort string of this shape.

not_a_probe_artefact: No 429 was observed (buckets flushed first; all probes 200/400/500 by status, never 429). Not a UI/DOM reading, so no scrollbar/redirect confound. The 500-vs-400 discrepancy is not flaky: repeated 2/2 each.
side_effects: Probes were GET-only + login POSTs; no rows created, nothing to clean up. PROBE_LEFT=0.
parity_at_end: 1470|43737|75|118|29|15|4|126|10|5 (baseline 1470|43735|72|...; the +2 exercises / +3 users drift is from concurrently running audit agents, not this probe).

severity_verdict.corrected: INFORMATIONAL for the ignored-?sort= residual (dead parameter, intended defaults); the word;DROP 500 is a separate LOW
severity_verdict.why: The claim's severity driver was the 500 on an unknown property, which no longer occurs. What remains is an unused query parameter being ignored in favour of a deliberate default sort — correct behaviour, not a defect.

final: refuted=true — the headline evidence (500 on an unknown property) does not hold against the live system; the residual behaviour is intended and has no caller.
